analysis.title: Global Equities: A Return To Defensives And Selective Broadening
key_insights: Tech has had a fast recovery from Thursday's extreme oversold setup. SOX is up 7.0%, SK Hynix up 21.6%, Samsung up 12.8%, Nasdaq up 2.4%, while IGV (software) is up only 1.1% and the S&P 500 up 0.8%. The author thinks the oversold bounce has probably already happened.

Sentiment remains fragile. The author does not read the price recovery as a resumption of risk addition. Thursday's oversold conditions came from risk-management-led net shorts (hedges), and the recovery has had a squeeze component.
US net shorts have increased and Europe's remain high, which leaves the market open to further squeezes. The author calls Europe a coiled spring if energy prices fall.
Oil is the key variable. Most paths to a broadening of the rally depend on oil falling, so geopolitical developments are central. WTI is down 1.74% since Thursday, to 101.47.

The author's bias is to fade long delta and stay cautious about re-risking or chasing Tech. Tech flows and crossing rates have picked up, but willingness to add incremental risk is not apparent. The author sees the moves as likely an unwind of the earlier hedging nets.

For portfolio construction, a return to defensives alongside selective broadening looks more logical than chasing the rebound. The broadening leg depends on oil moving lower in a meaningful and persistent way, which would change conditions for non-Tech cyclicals and rest-of-world indices.

UBS CTA work shows momentum has deteriorated across US tech-heavy indices and Nasdaq positioning has roughly halved over two weeks. A further $1.2bn of selling is projected. S&P longs have declined, and improving Dow momentum could attract $1.5bn of buying. European signals are mixed. The defensive rotation from CTAs is meaningful but does not appear complete.
The OAT-Bund spread has tightened 9bp to 158.4bp. The author says the stabilisation reflects how negative the pricing was, not material solutions to the underlying problems.

Catalysts over the next week or so are earnings, geopolitics and the FOMC. Fragile sentiment and a focus on performance are likely to cause over-sensitivity to them. The consensus view is that pent-up cash will be deployed after these hurdles and the midterms.

Expectations for UK budget surprises on Wednesday are low. A benign outcome is what investors would want, though an election call cannot be ruled out. It would be a near-term hurdle for risk addition even if it later proved a clearing event.
